questions.question: The speed of a car is 1(1)/(5) times the speed of a bus. A train covers 1200 km in 15 hours. How much distance will the car cover in 7 hours if the speed of the bus is 1(1)/(4) times the speed of the train?
questions.solution:
Given:

The speed of a car is 1(1)/(5) i.e 6/5 times the speed of a bus.

The train covers 1200 km in 15 hours.

The bus is 1(1)/(4) i.e. 5/4 times the speed of the train.

Concept used:

Time × Speed = Distance

Calculation:

Speed of the train = 1200/15 = 80 km/h

Speed of the bus = 80 × 5/4 = 100 km/h

Speed of the car = 100 × 6/5 = 120 kmph

Now, the distance covered by the car in 7 hours = 120 × 7 = 840 km

∴ The car will cover a distance of 840 km in 7 hours.

questions.question: If the simple interest for five years is equal is 35% of the principal, that rate of interest is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The simple interest for five years is equal is 35% of the principal.

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the principal and rate of interest be P and R% per annum respectively.

According to the question,

(P × R × 5)/100 = P × 35%

⇒ (R × 5) = 35 (∵ P ≠ 0)

⇒ R = 35/5

⇒ R = 7

∴ The rate of interest is 7% per annum.

questions.question: Which is the smallest number which when divided by 6, 8 and 10 leaves remainders 4, 6 and 8, respectively?
questions.solution:
Given:

The smallest number which when divided by 6, 8 and 10 leaves remainders 4, 6 and 8, respectively

Concept used:

LCM is the smallest common multiple of two or more numbers.

Calculation:

LCM (6, 8, 10) = 120

The smallest number divided by 6, 8, and 10 = 120

So we get,

⇒ 6 - 4 = 2

⇒ 8 - 6 = 2

⇒ 10 - 8 = 2

Now, the required number = 120 - 2 = 118

**∴ 118 is the smallest number which when divided by 6, 8 and 10 leaves the remaining 4, 6 and 8, respectively.**

questions.question: A and B together can complete a certain work in 20 days, B and C together can complete it in 30 days and C and A together can complete it in 24 days. In how many days will A alone complete (7)/(12) part of the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B together can complete a certain work in 20 days, B and C together can complete it in 30 days and C and A together can complete it in 24 days.

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency (Work done per hour) × Total time taken

Calculation:

LCM (20, 30, 24) = 120

Let the total work be the LCM of the time taken by different workers.

So, total work = 120 units

Let the efficiencies of A, B, and C be represented by A, B, and C.

According to the question,

A + B = 120/20

⇒ A + B = 6 ....(1)

B + C = 120/30

⇒ B + C = 4 ....(2)

A + C = 120/24

⇒ A + C = 5 ....(3)

(1) + (2) + (3),

2(A + B + C) = 6 + 4 + 5

⇒ A + B + C = 7.5 ....(4)

(4) - (2),

A + B + C - B - C = 7.5 - 4

⇒ A = 3.5

Now, A alone will complete (7)/(12) part of the same work in

⇒ ((7)/(12) × 120)/3.5

⇒ 20 days

**∴ A alone will complete (7)/(12) part of the same work in 20 days.**

questions.question: A can complete a project in 10 days and B can complete the same project in 15 days. A and B start working on the project together and A quit 5 days before the project is completed. In how many days is the project completed?
questions.solution:
Given:

A can complete a project in 10 days and B can complete the same project in 15 days. 

A and B start working on the project together and A quit 5 days before the project is completed. 

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency (Work done per hour) × Total time taken

Calculation:

LCM (10, 15) = 30

Let the total project be the LCM of the time taken by different workers.

So, total project = 30 units

A's efficiency = 30/10 = 3 unit per day

B's efficiency = 30/15 = 2 unit per day

Let in N days the project be completed.

According to the question,

3 × (N - 5) + 2 × N = 30

⇒ 3N - 15 + 2N = 30

⇒ 5N = 15 + 30

⇒ N = 45/5

⇒ N = 9

∴ The project is completed in 9 days.

questions.question: A man sold an almirah for ₹960 at a loss of 4%. He then sold a folding bed for ₹840 at a profit of 20%. Find his profit or loss.
questions.solution:
Given:

A man sold an almirah for ₹960 at a loss of 4%. 

He then sold a folding bed for ₹840 at a profit of 20%.

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the almirah and folding bed be P and Q respectively.

According to the question,

P - P × 4% = 960

⇒ 0.96P = 960

⇒ N = 960/0.96

⇒ N = 1000

According to the question,

Q + Q × 20% = 840

⇒ 1.2Q = 840

⇒ Q = 840/1.2

⇒ Q = 700

Total cost price of two of these articles = 1000 + 700 = Rs. 1700

Total selling price of two of these articles = 960 + 840 = Rs. 1800

Now, his profit = 1800 - 1700 = Rs. 100

∴ His profit is Rs. 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**In case of Almirah, we have

Loss% = 4% = 1/25

Ratio of C.P. to S.P. = 25 : 24

⇒ 24 unit = Rs. 960

⇒ 25 units = (960/24) × 25 = Rs. 1000

In case of folding bed, we have

Profit % = 20% = 1/5

Ratio of C.P. to S.P. = 5 : 6

⇒ 6 units = Rs. 840

⇒ 5 units = (840/6) × 5 = Rs. 700

Now, Total C.P. = Rs. 1000 + Rs. 700 = Rs. 1700

Total S.P. = Rs. 960 + Rs. 840 = Rs. 1800

Profit = 1800 - 1700 = Rs. 100

∴ His profit is Rs. 100.
